rows.abstract: With the upgraded pension of the city and municipal judges, they will be able to live comfortable and decent lives after having devoted the fruitful years of their life to the dispensation of justice.

rows.abstract: Rationale: The ordinary citizen should not be compelled to comply with the compulsory financing scheme as prescribed by PD No. 217. The scheme is not only burdensome but also oppressive.

rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING THAT A YEAR SHALL BE COUNTED AS CONTAINING THREE HUNDRED SIXTY DAYS IN COMPUTING THE LENGTH OF ACTIVE MILITARY SERVICE IN THE ARMED FORCES OF THE PHILIPPINES, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE REPUBLIC ACT NO. 6948, ENTITLED, `AN ACT STANDARDIZING AND UPGRADING THE BENEFITS FOR MILITARY VETERANS AND THEIR DEPENDENTS'
rows.abstract: With the proposal, a six-year term military service will only require 2.160 days, instead of the prescribed 2, 190 days (RA6948), for a veteran to be entitled to pension benefits.
rows.status: Business for the day on 1999-04-27

rows.author: B012
rows.title_full: AN ACT GRANTING UNTO ALL GSIS RETIREES A PRIVILEGE TO BORROW FROM THE GSIS A PENSION LOAN EQUIVALENT TO NOT MORE THAN SIX (6) MONTHS PENSION
rows.abstract: Seeks to extend financial assistance to GSIS retirees for them to cope with the economic crunch, considering their dependence on their monthly pension.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on GOVERNMENT ENTERPRISES AND PRIVATIZATION since 1999-01-18

rows.author: C022
rows.title_full: AN ACT ABOLISHING DEATH PENALTY IN THE PHILIPPINES
rows.abstract: Rationale: The death  penalty (1) precludes reparation for a wrongful conviction; (2) hampers preventive and remedial action; (3) dares, rather than deters, hardened criminals; (4) glamorizes crime for the mentally unstable; and (5) breeds callous judges and counsels. More importantly, capital punishment is incompatible with the self-respect of a civilized nation.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on JUSTICE since 1999-01-18
